discussion.title: Single-request reversal and fixed behavioral acceptance
discussion.status: Concrete design for independent review; scope approved, implementation held
discussion.summary: Prepare the same retained window and requested section, request activation once, then key/front ordering in the same invocation. Two focused guests must qualify before three separately declared complete ordinary guests. Both sets use identical signed candidate bytes with diagnostics disabled. A qualified recurrence rejects reversal. Any other required failure or unavailable evidence stops acceptance and all later slots. Raw transport failures remain failures. A complete pass supports only the declared sample; native cause and ownership remain unresolved. No new signed subject, build or guest exists. Independent review and every earned integration precede implementation/runtime.

diagrams.title: Prepare one window, activate once, then order it
diagrams.caption: Proposed synchronous application order, including readiness failure. The window is constructed and navigation applied before activation. A return does not imply activation completed; the OS may decline. Launch, reopen and both menu callers share this owner. No retry, yielding or deferral is added.

diagrams.title: Two focused guests before three complete ordinary guests
diagrams.caption: Proposed finite convention: E01/E02 and A01/A02/A03 are fresh, serial slots using one frozen candidate with diagnostics disabled. Any required failure or unavailable evidence stops all later slots. Qualified recurrence takes precedence over later evidence failures. All outcomes retain audit and exact cleanup; passing covers only that sample. There is no baseline, replacement or cap expansion.
